title: Peiminine attenuates inflammatory bowel disease by suppressing TLR4 mediated NFkB pathway: an integrated network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Shah, Bhagyabhumi; Sharma, Aditi; Patel, Mansi; Shah, Umang; Parekh, Nikunj; Solanki, Nilay
one_liner_zh: 该文研究贝母素甲通过TLR4/NFkB通路缓解炎症性肠病，涉及网络药理学和分子对接，但核心是药物抗炎机制，无蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease are two of the complex and recurring inflammatory conditions that comprise inflammatory bowel disease. There are currently relatively few therapeutic alternatives available for its treatment, and those that are available have serious side effects. It is also in a very progressive and prevalent phase. Therefore, it is necessary to find safer and more effective therapeutics for its treatment. Targeting different molecular pathways, peiminine has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory qualities. Integrated network pharmacology and molecular docking depicted various targets, amongst them NFkB and TNF-alpha were the targets where peiminine elicited maximum binding affinity. Validating the in silico data, further in in vivo study, mice were randomly allocated into six groups: Normal control (NC), Disease control (DC-TNBS, 2,4,6-trinitrobenzene sulfonic acid), STD (TNBS + sulfasalazine 100 mg/kg, p.o.), PEI1, PEI2 & PEI3 (TNBS + Peiminine 1, 2.5, & 5 mg/kg, p.o.), respectively. A sharp fall in disease activity index (DAI) and changes in histopathological examination revealed the colonoprotective effect of peiminine. It also depicted anti-oxidant activity through reducing the levels of myeloperoxidase (MPO) and nitric oxide (NO) and elevating superoxide dismutase (SOD), and catalase (CAT). It downregulated various pro-inflammatory mediators such as tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in in vitro and in vivo studies, depicting its anti-inflammatory activity. Peiminine has also been shown to have strong anti-inflammatory properties by downregulating the gene expression of TLR4 (1.96-fold), NFkB (1.70-fold), iNOS (1.27-fold), COX-2 (2.40-fold), and IL-1beta (0.80-fold). Meanwhile, it increases the expression of anti-inflammatory mediator IL-10 (2.55-fold). Collectively, peiminine likely decreased colon damage and TNBS-induced colitis through the TLR4-mediated NFkB pathway.
abstract_zh: 溃疡性结肠炎和克罗恩病是构成炎症性肠病的两种复杂且复发性炎症疾病。目前可用于其治疗的替代疗法相对较少，且现有疗法具有严重副作用。该病也处于高度进展和流行阶段。因此，有必要寻找更安全、更有效的治疗药物。通过靶向不同分子通路，贝母素（peiminine）具有抗氧化和抗炎特性。整合网络药理学和分子对接（molecular docking）揭示了多个靶点，其中NFkB和TNF-alpha是贝母素表现出最大结合亲和力的靶点。为验证计算机模拟数据，进一步在体内研究中，小鼠被随机分为六组：正常对照（NC）、疾病对照（DC-TNBS，2,4,6-三硝基苯磺酸）、标准治疗组（STD，TNBS + 柳氮磺吡啶100 mg/kg，口服）、PEI1、PEI2和PEI3（TNBS + 贝母素1、2.5和5 mg/kg，口服）。疾病活动指数（DAI）的急剧下降和组织病理学检查的变化揭示了贝母素的结肠保护作用。它还通过降低髓过氧化物酶（MPO）和一氧化氮（NO）水平，并升高超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）和过氧化氢酶（CAT）水平，表现出抗氧化活性。在体外和体内研究中，它下调了多种促炎介质，如肿瘤坏死因子-α（TNF-alpha）和白细胞介素-6（IL-6），表明其抗炎活性。贝母素还通过下调TLR4（1.96倍）、NFkB（1.70倍）、iNOS（1.27倍）、COX-2（2.40倍）和IL-1beta（0.80倍）的基因表达，显示出强效抗炎特性。同时，它增加了抗炎介质IL-10的表达（2.55倍）。总体而言，贝母素可能通过TLR4介导的NFkB通路减轻结肠损伤和TNBS诱导的结肠炎。
